meta.title: The First American Flag — Set 3
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Details on historical designs, Betsy Ross, and timeline changes of the U.S. flag.

questions.question: In what city did the famous seamstress Betsy Ross live?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Some people think it was a seamstress who lived in Philadelphia. Her name was Betsy Ross.'

questions.question: Historians know for sure exactly who sewed the very first American flag.
questions.explanation: False. The text states: 'Who made the first flag? No one knows for sure.'

questions.question: How many points did the stars have on Francis Hopkinson's flag?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The corner had 13 six-pointed stars on a patch of blue.'

questions.question: On today's U.S. flag, the stars are arranged in a round circle.
questions.explanation: False. Today's flag has stars arranged in rows, representing the 50 states.

questions.question: How many stripes are on the U.S. flag today?
questions.explanation: Today's U.S. flag has 13 stripes representing the original 13 states.

questions.question: The corner patch of the flag contains white stars on a background of _______.
questions.hint: The color of the sky on a sunny day.
questions.explanation: The stars are placed on a blue field or patch in the top corner of the flag.

questions.question: By 1795, after new states joined, how many stars and stripes did the flag have?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'By 1795, the flag had 15 stars and 15 stripes' as new states were added.

questions.question: Sort these names based on whether they are associated with Flag Making/Designing or represent Other entities in the story:
questions.explanation: Betsy Ross and Francis Hopkinson are associated with making or designing the flag. Hawaii is a state, and George Washington was an early leader.

questions.question: On June 14, 1777, 'Hopkinson's flag' became the first official flag of the United States.
questions.explanation: True. The text explains: 'On June 14, 1777, “Hopkinson’s flag” became the first flag of the United States.'

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe how stars were placed on some old flags:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The stars were in rows.' Some old flags used straight rows.

questions.question: What did the country decide to do in 1818 when there were 20 states?
options: Go back to a flag with 13 stripes and add a star for each new state
Remove all red stripes and make the flag solid blue
Stop using stars on the flag
questions.explanation: The text states: 'By 1818, there were 20 states... So, the country went back to a flag with 13 stripes. A star was added for each new state.'

questions.question: The flag got its 50th star on July 4, _______.
questions.explanation: Hawaii became the 50th state, and its star was added to the flag on July 4, 1960.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe what some old flags had:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Some old flags had circles.' The stars were placed in circular patterns.

questions.question: Francis Hopkinson's flag design had 13 red and white stripes and 13 six-pointed stars on blue.
questions.explanation: True. The text explains: 'His flag had 13 red and white stripes. The corner had 13 six-pointed stars on a patch of blue.'

questions.question: Why did early flags have stars in different patterns, like circles or rows?
options: Because there was no single rule about how to arrange the stars as states joined
Because early leaders forgot how to sew straight lines
Because states wanted to design their own private flags
Because seamstresses wanted to show off different styles
questions.explanation: The text shows that as states were added, stars were placed in circles or rows depending on the maker, before a final standard row design was chosen.
